question: Find the equation of the line passing through the points $A(1,2,-1)$ and $B(4,0,5)$ in both vector and Cartesian form. Also find the direction cosines of the line.

options.A:
Vector form: $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)+\lambda(3\hat i-2\hat j+6\hat k)$
Cartesian form: $\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y-2}{-2}=\frac{z+1}{6}$
Direction cosines: $\left(\frac{3}{7},-\frac{2}{7},\frac{6}{7}\right)$
options.B:
Vector form: $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)+\lambda(3\hat i+2\hat j+6\hat k)$
Cartesian form: $\frac{x-1}{3}=\frac{y-2}{2}=\frac{z+1}{6}$
Direction cosines: $\left(\frac{3}{7},\frac{2}{7},\frac{6}{7}\right)$
options.C:
Vector form: $\vec r=(4\hat i+5\hat k)+\lambda(3\hat i-2\hat j+6\hat k)$
Cartesian form: $\frac{x-4}{3}=\frac{y}{-2}=\frac{z-5}{6}$
Direction cosines: $\left(\frac{3}{5},-\frac{2}{5},\frac{6}{5}\right)$
options.D:
Vector form: $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j-\hat k)+\lambda(4\hat i-2\hat j+5\hat k)$
Cartesian form: $\frac{x-1}{4}=\frac{y-2}{-2}=\frac{z+1}{5}$
Direction cosines: $\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{45}},-\frac{2}{\sqrt{45}},\frac{5}{\sqrt{45}}\right)$
